arxiv-2103-13371.title: Interplay between transport and quantum coherences in free fermionic systems
arxiv-2103-13371.creator: Tony Jin, Tristan Gautié, Alexandre Krajenbrink, Paola Ruggiero, Takato Yoshimura
arxiv-2103-13371.description: Abstract We study the quench dynamics in free fermionic systems in the prototypical bipartitioning protocol obtained by joining two semi-infinite subsystems prepared in different states, aiming at understanding the interplay between quantum coherences in space in the initial state and transport properties. Our findings reveal that, under reasonable assumptions, the more correlated the initial state, the slower the transport is.

arxiv-2211-16415.title: Distributed Computation of Exact Average Degree and Network Size in Finite Number of Steps under Quantized Communication
arxiv-2211-16415.creator: Apostolos I. Rikos, Themistoklis Charalambous, Christoforos N. Hadjicostis, Karl H. Johansson
arxiv-2211-16415.description: Abstract We consider the problems of computing the average degree and the size of a given network in a distributed fashion under quantized communication. We present two distributed algorithms which rely on quantized operation (i.e., nodes process and transmit quantized messages), and are able to calculate the exact solutions in a finite number of steps.

arxiv-2508-06143.title: Turbulence in the Geomagnetic Field at Earth Surface
arxiv-2508-06143.creator: Mingshu Zhao, Xiaoping Zeng, Yunfang Lin
arxiv-2508-06143.description: Abstract We investigated turbulence-like behavior in the geomagnetic field using ground-based magnetic observatory data across China. Through analysis of spatial and temporal structure functions, we find power-law scaling consistent with Kolmogorov-like turbulence under extended self-similarity. We also identify significant correlations between vertical geomagnetic field variations and large earthquakes.

arxiv-2511-09078.title: Nuclear shape dynamics in low-energy heavy-ion reactions

arxiv-2511-09078.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by \firstname Kouichi \lastname Hagino. We discuss recent theoretical developments in low-energy heavy-ion reactions. To this end, we put emphasis on a viewpoint of probing nuclear shapes with heavy-ion reactions. We first discuss a single-channel problem with an optical potential model. We particularly discuss a microscopic modeling of the imaginary part of an optical potential as well as a visualization of quantum interference phenomena observed in heavy-ion elastic scattering.

pmc-13411277.title: Histological and molecular characterization of bone integrity in osteogenesis imperfecta: a case series across genetic subtypes
pmc-13411277.creator: Zhiming Wu, Suzanne den Haan, Helen E King, Wouter H Nijhuis, Harrie Weinans, Anne J Spaans, Ralph Sakkers, Kelly Warmink
pmc-13411277.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a genetically heterogeneous skeletal disorder characterized by bone fragility and variable clinical severity. However, how molecular defects translate into alterations of bone microstructure and composition across OI subtypes remains incompletely understood. In this case series, we systematically evaluated cortical bone integrity in patients with OI types 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, and 14 using histological and molecular approaches, including Raman spectroscopy, and compared findings with non-OI controls.
